thick bakery style chocolate chip cookies🍪🍫 Ingredients: 170g (3/4 cup) unsalted butter, cold and cubed 150g (3/4 cup) brown sugar 70g (1/3 cup) granulated sugar 1 egg + 1 egg yolk 2 tsp vanilla 300g (2 1/2 cups) all purpose flour 1 tbsp cornstarch 1/2 tsp baking soda 1/4 tsp baking powder 3/4 tsp salt 250g (1 1/2 cups) chocolate chips  Flakey sea salt (optional) Instructions:  1. In a large bowl, combine the butter, brown sugar, and white sugar. Mix until smooth and well combined. Do not cream. 2. Add the egg, egg yolk, and vanilla, then mix until fully incorporated. 3. Add the dry ingredients (flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda, and salt) and fold until just combined. 4. Fold in the chocolate chips or chunks until evenly distributed. Do not overmix. 5. Divide the dough into 150g portions and shape each into a rough ball. 6. Place the dough balls on a lined tray, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight. 7. Bake in a preheated 190°C (375°F) oven for 13-16 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the centers are still slightly soft. 8. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking tray for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. If desired, sprinkle with flaky sea salt and let cool for about 15 minutes before serving. Enjoy! Note: This recipe made 6 cookies weighing 150g each and 1 cookie weighing 100g🍪🤎 #baking #cookies #chocolatechipcookies #Recipe #nyccookies

Nutella bombolini ✨ Ingredients  Donuts - 435g bread flour (3 cups + 2 tbsp) - 68g granulated sugar (1/3 cup) - 185g whole milk (3/4 cup) - 60g unsalted butter, softened (4 tbsp) - 7g active dry yeast (2 1/4 tsp) - 2 large eggs - 1 tsp vanilla extract  - 1/2 tsp salt - Canola oil for frying Filling/topping - 7.7 oz Nutella  - Granulated sugar (to cover donuts) Instructions  - In a bowl, combine warm milk and 1 tbsp sugar. Sprinkle yeast over the top, stir lightly, and let sit 5–10 minutes until foamy. - Add eggs, 1/3 cup sugar, vanilla extract and mix again until well combined. - Add flour to mixture. Mix until a rough dough forms. - Begin kneading. Once the dough starts to come together, gradually add the softened butter (1 tbsp at a time), kneading until fully incorporated before adding more. - Continue kneading 8–10 minutes by hand or 5–6 minutes in a stand mixer, until smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky. - Transfer dough to a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise 1–1½ hours, or until doubled in size. - Punch down dough and separate into 12 balls (weighing 65g each) - Place onto parchment lined tray cover loosely and let rise 30–40 minutes, until puffy. - In a large skillet heat oil to 325–335°F (aim for 330°F) - Fry 2–3 minutes per side - Flip every 30–45 seconds for even color - Fry until golden brown - Remove donuts from oil place onto a wire rack  - Toss in sugar until fully coated - Poke a hole in the top of each donut - Pipe in Nutella filling until slightly heavy - Serve & enjoy!  • • • #Recipe #donuts #baking #bakingrecipe

PART 1/2 Meet Beau. A 6-year-old German Shepherd / Great Pyrenees mix with a serious bite history. Beau had bitten his owner multiple times, a family friend, and during his last vet visit, he attempted to bite both staff and the veterinarian. He was overwhelmed, unsafe, and heading down a path with very few options left. Thankfully, his owners didn’t give up. They reached out and committed to a 6-week behavior modification board & train. After 5 weeks of structured behavior work, obedience, and muzzle conditioning, we returned to the same veterinary clinic that Beau struggled in before training. This was a high-stakes moment. There were multiple bite attempts, but here’s the difference: everyone stayed calm, neutral, and communicative. That changed everything. Was it perfect? No. Was Beau safer, more manageable, and able to be treated for a painful bacterial infection in his paw? Yes. Handling a 100+ lb dog with bite history is no small task. Huge respect to my apprentice Kevin and Beau’s owner for staying consistent and showing up when it mattered most. When a dog has a bite history, should they be written off as “dangerous,” or does the responsibility fall on the owner to step up, provide structure, and do the hard work instead of giving up? #DogTraining #dogs #dogtrainer #dogsoftiktok #behaviormod
